cmd.help.title: Commands:
cmd.help.body:
/help — show this help
/reset — archive this chat's session and start fresh
/model [id] — show or set the model for this chat
/status — session turns, current model, service uptime
/lang [code] — show or set the reply language
/learn memory <text> | /learn skill <slug> :: <desc> :: <body> — record an experience
/reflect [daily|weekly|monthly] — generate the reflect skeleton (facts only)
/evolution — self-evolution loop status
/cron [add [message|prompt] <spec> :: <text> | del <id>] — natural-language cron jobs
/checkpoint [restore <id>] — file checkpoints + rollback (write_file/edit_file)
cmd.learn.usage:
/learn memory <text>
/learn skill <slug> :: <description> :: <body>
lint gate + skill pre-screen run before any write (slug: a-z0-9._-)
cmd.evolution.head: evolution: {enabled} · cron daily {daily_at} · weekly {weekly_day} · monthly day {monthly_day}
cmd.cron.usage:
/cron
/cron add [message|prompt] <spec> :: <text>
/cron del <id>
spec: every 30m | daily 08:00 | weekly mon 08:00 | once YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (Beijing time)
cmd.cron.empty: no cron jobs — add one: /cron add daily 08:00 :: drink water
cmd.checkpoint.usage:
/checkpoint — list recent file checkpoints
/checkpoint restore <id> — put that file back

auth.title: Your authority
auth.lead: Hold the seal to authorise a read-only review preview. This preview does not connect to any service, sends nothing and executes nothing.
auth.sealTip: Hold to authorise a read-only preview
auth.hintIdle: Press and hold · release early to cancel
auth.resultBody: Authorised locally for this preview only. It does not connect to a service and executes no action; in the product a real write still requires its own human approval every time.
auth.med.situation.name: Situation
auth.med.situation.body: Everything I watch stays on this machine. Signals are gathered locally, compared against your baselines, and never shipped to a third party.
auth.med.memory.name: Memory
auth.med.memory.body: Your memory is plain text you own — copyable, diffable, restorable onto another machine, or carried into a different kernel entirely.
auth.med.constitution.name: Constitution
auth.med.constitution.body: Your rules are injected as a constitution, not a suggestion: free forever, credentials never echoed, no write without approval.
auth.med.authority.name: Authority
auth.med.authority.body: Every consequential action reaches a human gate. I can prepare, preview and recommend — I cannot wave anything through myself.
ex.lead: Market reads are keyless. Orders exist only as plans: this panel is where you approve or reject them — the model's execute step receives a plan id and can never approve its own plan. Withdrawals and on-chain transfers do not exist in this product at all.
ex.disc.fees: The product is permanently free, but exchange fees and on-chain gas are not zero: you settle them yourself with the exchange or the chain.
ex.disc.advice: Nothing on this panel is investment advice.
ex.disc.risk: Trading risk is borne by you: you are responsible for the outcome of any trade you make.
ex.disc.creds: Credentials stay on this machine (secrets.env) and are never echoed into chats, logs or documents.
ex.unavailable: exchange capability not available yet — this build has no exchange backend block
ex.probe.idle: pick a venue, then press FETCH QUOTE

ex.plans.empty: no plans waiting — plans are created by exchange_prepare_order; nothing here executes by itself

act.start: Welcome — 3 steps to activate: 1) set the console access token, 2) set the bot token and the owner allowlist, 3) point the model endpoint. Fix each row below, or run in a terminal:
act.restartConfirm: Restart the chat service now? Bot token / allowlist / tool changes take effect after a restart.
act.restartNoTmux: no service session to restart (tmux) — start it first
act.restartTimeout: the service did not report running within 20s — check the Overview panels
act.item.tg_allowlist: Users allowed to talk to the bot
act.hint.web_token: opens the console write gate — presence only, never echoed

act.hint.tg_allowlist: numeric Telegram user ids, comma separated — who may talk to the bot
act.hint.model_endpoint: OpenAI-compatible base URL — it must answer /models
act.hint.service: the bot runs inside the chat service — restart it after credential changes
onb.accessHint: The access token is WEB_TOKEN — the unlock password for this console, written into secrets.env when you installed. Paste it once below and this browser remembers it; after that saving settings, approvals and service restarts all work. It cannot be changed from this page (that would lock you out): to rotate it, edit WEB_TOKEN in secrets.env, then paste the new value here.
onb.tgSwap: Switching to a different bot (3 steps)
onb.tgStep1: In Telegram, open @BotFather and send /newbot (or /token for an existing bot) to get the new bot's token.
onb.tgStep2: Paste that token into "Telegram bot token" above and press SET.
onb.tgStep3: Press "RESTART CHAT SERVICE" below so the service picks the new token up.
onb.tgAllow: If you switched bots, also update "Users allowed to talk to the bot" with your own numeric Telegram user ID: send any message to @userinfobot or @getmyid_bot (either one works) and it replies with your ID.
